notes.title: 0.187.5 - Lords of the Ring
notes.content:
A brand new rings
When looking from telescopic distance the Rings of Saturn appear to be flat and monotonous, but they are not such up-close.

I took a good look at the map of the rings the game uses, and I found it quite bland. This release fixes that, with brand new map of the rings. You will now encounter different, distinct regions - places where there are veins of minerals and quite barren, regions of tiny ringroids and huge concentrations big rocks. There is a lot of variety now and you should find that regions are different, even when they made from the same water ice.

Gravimetric scanner will be now much more useful - at least until you learn how to distinguish the field just by observing the movement of the ringroidroids. You can also now spot and visit huge, hundred of kilometres long features of the rings and see them up close.

Soak tests to ensure stability
Nothing breaks the game as much as unexpected crashes. Games are, ultimately, complex pieces of software and many things can go wrong on many levels. To ensure that game is stable I'm running soak tests - rigging the in-game NPC AI to players ship and let it mine on hours on hours. Current version went through over 20 hours of testing without crash, so I hope we managed to find all the problems.

More bugs fixed
As with every release, I try to patch up every problem you come across and report. Here is a list of what's fixed in this one:

 Phage stations won't get hostile anymore if you burn them a bit with your thrusters while docking.
 Fixed pixel doubling setting to not require game restart.
 Fixed adrenaline booster to work again.
 Gravimetric scanner had much too many noise, making the readings unusable in some regions of the rings.
 Fixed a bug in maintenance drones that caused them to be affected by your mechanic jury-rigging the ship.
 Fixed some visual glitches.
 Improved collision detection and AI path-finding, so ships will not ram so readily.
 Key prompt for comms and accompanying chat bubble would disappear or appear at wrong moments. 
 You found couple of conditions that caused crashes, and I patched them up.

notes.title: 0.186.13 - Leaky Reactor
notes.content:
This is a bugfix patch, fixing up couple of bugs you discovered in the latest release. Bugs fixed:

 NPC ship executing maneuvers at the very edge of simulation range could crash the game.
 Changed the way game writes logs to ensure that we always have something to work with when you report a crash.
 Patched up couple of memory leaks.
 Changed the exit-to-desktop code to make sure it closes all resources before exiting.

notes.title: 0.186.9 - Shortfall of Gravitas
notes.content:
Today I present you a combined content and bugfix patch. I feel that it's important for Early Access title to address all the known bugs as fast as possible, but I think it's equally important to add some new content, so players who didn't hit the bugs will get something out of it.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33358845/8db7ccebac87da888bdec190d39c8ba2699b42fb.gif

Additional upgrades and upgrade changes
A big feature of Shortfall of Gravitas is addition of gimbaled engine mechanics. Thruster gimbals are the real-world technology that allows the rockets to fly - the exhaust can be tilted, providing additional layer of control. This is a multi-stage enhancement: I needed to add a other type of thruster, make sure that autopilot and AI understands that thurster and it's capabilities, and finally - research and develop actual thruster you can buy.

With version 0.186.9 you can equip your ship with Nuclear Assisted Gimbaled Hall Effect Thruster RCS. This is first in the line of vectored thrust that will come in the game. Despite being weaker than most competition and having extraordinary power requirements, NAGHET provides you with ability to vector your exhaust up to 20 degrees, yielding excellent maneuverability (for it's thrust). The downsides are higher price and susceptibility to misalignment.

Gravimetric drone got an overhaul. I made sure that gravimetric drone readouts are accurate and actually readable on all ships. You can now use the drone to guide you to interesting parts of the Rings, as it was supposed to be in the first place.

Bugs fixed
You found many bugs, and I did my best to fix all of them. Here is the list of patches applied:

 Made the visual cues for combat/discovery subtler, so they won't obscure HUD anymore.
 You no-longer can fix the ship up into negative damage, causing unexpected behaviour.
 Fine-tuned thermal damage to thrusters, so well-aimed hit from powerful laser will not send ships spinning so easily.
 Jury-rig mechanics skill was re-balanced. Previously most mechanics you could hire hit the repair cap too soon, making the higher levels of skill useless.
 Fixed appearance of some ships, that were missing vital parts.
 Mouse control of menus could be obscured by invisible objects at Enceladus, making parts of the menus unusable after returning from dive, opening crew menu and similar.
 Fine-tuned font setting for Russian, Korean and Chinese (simplified and traditional) translations, so descriptions at Enceladus don't obscure one-another.
 Removed the lags from settings menu. Have lags for sale now.
 Fixed couple of memory leaks.
 Mining ships again visible on menu screen and credits.
 Fixed a bug in adaptive/military autopilot that caused it to behave worse if it gathered weird data for it's turning feedback loop. As result, said autopilots now fly much smoother.
 Tuned the Eagle Prospector HUD that could flicker if you had big remass tanks and broke your on-board computer just a bit.
 Fixed NPMP engine so it can be replaced now at normal price.
 Fixed a bug that caused guiding drone to work even if it's not mounted on the ship.
 Ships you bought are no-longer visible on the dealer's list.

notes.title: 0.185.5 - Fables for Robots
notes.content:
In our recent community vote over discrord.gg/dv you decided that I should split my time equally between adding ship upgrades and fleshing out the story of the game. This content patch adds both.

New story elements
With this upgrade we started fleshing out one of the main story arcs with the game. The phage station you could encounter earlier is no longer mute and will contact you, providing dialog and opportunities. This is just a introduction to new faction you can encounter now, and will be fleshed out further - in following days. There is also an additional secret you can discover in the rings.

Additional upgrades
You can now purchase a gravimetric drone that will allow you to see the subtle differences in gravitational fields of the Rings, guiding you to denser and more interesting areas.

Bugs fixed
As with every update, I fix couple of bugs and add some additional features:
 Fixed a memory leak in storyteller module that could lead to crashes when diving for long times.
 Improved performance around the phage-class stations and it's events.
 Fixed inconsistent upgrade descriptions.
 Improved compatibility for Intel-family graphics cards operating on older drivers.
 Fixes display of moonlet's shadow.
 Added new special effect for crew bio screen.
Road ahead
We are currently filling in the content. You can expect the upgrades to be frequent and incremental, providing new upgrades, ships and story multiple times a week. With previous update the balance was tipped to the upgrade side, so you can expect that I'll focus on story elements, dialog trees and encounters for next week.

notes.title: 0.181.5 - Shiny Core
notes.content:
This is a bugfix patch. Changelog:

 Geologist will no-longer forget prices if you have microseismic drone.
 Guiding drone system won't attempt to track ore chunks in cargo holds anymore.
 Additional performance improvements.

notes.title: 0.180.7 - Unlimited Power!
notes.content:
This release combines a critical bugfixes with extra features and upgrades. Most important for most players - I found and fixes an encounter that caused consistent crashes when diving in the rings. Fixing that will hopefully resolve all the recently reported in-flight crashes.

But there is more! We have new upgrade slot and new upgrades - 6 to be exact. Those are auxiliary power options, for these ships that just need extra juce to power their systems. We also have some extra tuning options requested by our community, 

Full changelog:

 Added new auxiliary ship slot and 6 upgrades to install in there.
 Reactor now shows clearly that it has too much pressure and is about to blow, and gives you few seconds to react. If you see intense plasma fires coming out of your reactor, it's time to fix this leak NOW. As a consequence, reactor will also not blow suddenly if you are just playing with OMS sliders.
 Fixed a bug that caused consistent crashes when flying.
 Fixed a bug that could freeze the game if you crashed badly in very dense area.
 Made the prospector grinder bit stiffer.

notes.title: 0.177.0 - Stability Dampers
notes.content:
This is a polishing / bugfix release, patching up all the problems discovered since last content updates. The highlight of this release are stability upgrades - I found a couple of ways you could crash the game and patched, hopefully, all of them.

I managed to slip in a new upgrade: the guiding recon drone, which allows you to input targets manually to your autonomous drone systems.

Detailed changelog:

 Added a new guiding drone upgrade.
 Upgrade menu will now show the control key for a upgrade, if available.
 Fixed crashes when repairing ships and skipping time at Enceladus.
 Fixed a bug that caused parts of Enceladus screen not to respond to mouse input immediately after a ringdive.
 Same ship can no-longer be listed twice in dealer menu.
 All the buttons are now available on main menu screen on devices with low resolution.
 Fixed thruster wear to work again as expected.
 Fine-tuned pirate dialog options, so it's now easier to successfully threaten a pirate.
 Fixed a bug in AI that caused terrified captains to shoot ignoring the engagement distance.
 Fine-tuned tutorials, so texts stay on screen long enough for everyone to read them.

notes.title: 0.175.3 - Xenon Burn
notes.content:
This is an enhancement release, expanding game mechanics, ships and story interactions. We had a community vote over our discord.gg/dv where we asked you about the direction of development - and you decided I should split my time equally between adding game elements and expanding the story. This is the first release that does so.

By popular demand, we took a close look at pirates and added ways you can interact with them peacefully. There are now options for intimidation and bribery.

We fine-tuned some core game mechanics:
Processed cargo storage is no longer a part of the mineral processing unit, but depends on the ship hull you are using.
Ships have now new interplanetary Xenon drives that they use for transit to and from the rings with minimal propellant usage. You can choose to use your main nuclear drive for the job, cutting the travel time significantly but arriving with less propellant. Ships will now track how much reactive mass is required for a quick return burn and how long will it take to reach Enceladus if you depart now.
The interlunar travel times - between Enceladus Prime and the Rings - were revised with new engines available. A quick burn with a nuclear rocket will take roughly 12 hours, while a xenon drive will need up to 4 days for the same travel. You can opt into faster travel times using your tuning menu back on Enceladus. This rebalances crew employment costs, as with fewer dives per month they are no longer negligible.

We got additional ship upgrades:
Eagle Prospector got an overhaul. There are two additional drone-only slots you can use, the grinder was tuned to better process ice and HUD was expanded with some additional information.
Geologists now will use your microseismic recon drone, if installed. Targetting or hovering over an ore chunk will focus your crew’s attention on a specific nugget. Analysis data is now displayed progressively, as geologist first estimates ringroids composition and price.

As with every release, this patch also comes with performance and stability improvements and various minor bugfixes. Full list of minor changes:

Improved AI performance.
Improved particle effect performance, especially laser ablation debris.
Fixed mass/weight unit conversions for Eagle Prospector HUD.
AI now better aware of thruster range and its danger to nearby ships.
Fixed a bug that caused crashes if you attempted to disable a system that was not installed.
Tutorial was reworded to make it clearer in autopilot match velocity sections.

notes.title: 0.173.5 - Guiding Hands
notes.content:
This is a enhancement release, adding new upgrades. Changelog:

 Fine-tuned haul drones to work better with Eagle Prospector.
 Added guiding recon drone upgrade, capable of directing autonomous drone systems to specific targets.
 Fine-tuned AI collision avoidance to be aware of the thruster range.
 Extended Rosatom-Antonov MPU to cover whole cargo hold in Eagle Prospector.
 Re-worded parts of tutorial to make it clearer.
 Processed cargo storage is now based on ship hull and no-longer part of MPU upgrade.
 Added two drone-only slots for the Eagle Prospector.
 Fine-tuned display of geologist information.
 Stability improvements.

notes.title: 0.171.14 - Apply Polish
notes.content:
This is a hotfix release, fixing couple of bugs and addressing other issues. Changelog:

 Adds visual feed, depth indicator and microseismic drone do Eagle Prospector HUD.
 Fixed a bug in AI that caused it to fly recklessly around ships.
 Improved performance of ship dealer.
 Old ships will still be spaceworthy, especially ones you encounter in the ring.
 Jury-rigging weapon systems works now.
 Fixed wear damage of engines.
 Availability of upgrade now refreshes every time your money changes.

notes.title: 0.171.10 - Units of Freedom
notes.content:
Feature complete
ΔV: Rings of Saturn released in Early Access 8 months ago, and in that time we have been steadily adding new features and gathering data points from you - our dear players. Now, these points of data make a beautiful line - as of today ΔV is officially feature-complete. Game has all the major features and major mechanics in place, all what's left is to hunt remaining bugs, polish up everything and - of course - add more content: ships, storylines, dialogs and upgrades.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33358845/516a1f83ad2f4d81e39328c93a72c4e69576862d.png

Ship dealer is here
The biggest new feature by far, and something everybody’s been waiting for, is the ship dealer.  This is your hub for buying and selling ships to fly.  Drop a pretty penny on that brand-new upgraded beauty off the showroom floor, or opt for a junker that will need a little love, but which could see you in a new ship, sooner.  Even buy a ship just for that awesome name, if you like.  

With the dealer in play, the Eagle Prospector is now available for purchase.  A lot has gone into polishing this girl up, with a lot of community effort going into feedback and fine-tuning. The Eagle is produced in the Free States of Earth, and comes with a free cheeseburger, side of cheesy bacon fries, a pickle, and a internal combustion mass driver in the glove box. It also has its own distinct HUD that, as an added bonus, measures everything in freedom units. She also comes with a beast of a grinder on her prow that will chew up asteroids, and a cargo bay markedly larger than the K37’s - big enough to swallow some smaller asteroids whole.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33358845/89216fbc9d711d363453a234639dccd1114cd513.png
Upgrade changes
Some changes were made to the way upgrade menus work, in order to prevent exploits, and this is a change to how things have been done previously, so it’s worth explaining.  Because you can buy a ship with damaged equipment for a lower cost, we can no longer let you swap out damaged equipment for the full price in the upgrade menu.  Instead, we refund less money for damaged equipment and charging you time, just as if you were replacing it via the repair menu.  If you switch back to that equipment, instead of getting a damaged part back, you are getting a part in pristine condition.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33358845/99cebd25cb1c1f09371e51441fef3ebf29f11e01.png
The road ahead
What next? We will focus now on adding more content. The ships you can fly, upgrades you can install, story events you might encounter and dialog trees to spice up your ringdives. There is still work ahead of us, but this time the progress will be smoother, with updates more frequent - yet smaller. Every few days you should see a new upgrade or event, so make sure you turn these auto upgrades on!

Best time to dive into The Rings!

notes.title: 0.157.0 - Not a Thruster
notes.content:
Fixing bugs is important, but adding features is where the fun is. This release adds a bunch of new visuals and hardware you can fit on your ships.

The Eagle Prospector radiators got a visual update. Eagle uses moving belt radiators - a track of high-specific-heat material that physically moves in and out of the reactor chamber to physically remove the heat. This design can remove much more heat than normal radiator, and the graphics of the Prospector now reflects that.

But why does it need to remove more heat? Eagle Prospector boasts a Yama SSR-16 40GW molten-uranium-core reactor to power it's twin main thrusters - and now you will be able to mount such molten-core reactors to all ships. They utilize rapidly spinning drums to keep the molten uranium at bay and a direct exchange of heat from fuel to reactive mass - a feat that keeps them both compact and powerful.

But what use is all this extra heat? You can now mount a plasma-thrower on your ship. It will take up to 18GW of super-heated plasma directly form your reactor and blast if forward to melt any asteroids directly in front of your ship. EINAT "Kzinti Lesson" Mk2 plasma thrower is definitely Not A (hastily retro-fitted) Thruster.

Not feeling like using plasma torches? Check out our new railgun. Compact and simple design is capable of both rapid fire and high muzzle velocities - but wears out faster than coilguns, and needs much more energy to deliver same hit. Good choice for a miner on the budget.

We are also thrilled to announce yet another community-supplied translation: Radek Poláček was kind enough to translate entire game to Czech!

Detailed changelog:

 Eagle Prospector now uses a visible moving-belt-radiators to match the game lore.
 New liquid-core reactor upgrades for your ship.
 New Kzinti Lesson Mk2 plasma thrower.
 Game now translated to Czech.
 Burning someone with thrusters or plasma throwers is now seen as hostile act.
 You can now buy railguns for your ships.
 Fixed a bug that caused ship details to reset during astrogation flight.

notes.title: 0.152.26 - Robots at Work
notes.content:
One of the paradigms we have for ΔV's development is "fix bugs first". We try to fix every bug we know of before adding new features. This should ensure that you get a polished and bug-free game at all times, even in Early Access stage. There are, of course, bugs that slip past us - either we don't find them soon enough, or the fixes we apply are not so effective as we thought. This why you get frequent bug-fixing releases, like this one.

This release addresses the issues we found over the weekend, but still manages to sneak in one autopilot improvement. We had reports that some players find the autopilot behaviour imperfect. When coasting through the rings and using the mouse to lock on rocks and ore, autopilot would attempt to put you to relative stop after each click. Many players found that disruptive, so we changed this behaviour. Clicking on an item will now preserve the relative velocity that you had.

Full changelog for this release:

 New autopilot controls for mouse. Clicking on an object will no-longer put you at relative stop by default, making it easier to mine with autopilot.
 Fixed a bug that could cause reactor overload and explosion after out-of-the-plane ring-hop.
 Player-controlled ships can no-longer be damaged during cutscenes.
 Fixed AI of the tug-ships, so they will pick up derelicts again,.
 Fixed a bug that caused impacts to be inaudible on player ships.

notes.content:
This is a re-balancing release. It changes the way kinetic damage is dealt to the ship, making the mass-drivers a valid option for ship-to-ship combat. Breached reactor core will now have lower critical temperature, and this in turn makes it a lot easier to cause ship explosion with kinetic damage.

The upgrade and tuning screens got an face-lift. They are more readable, and the charts you see as part of simulation will now display exact values. You also get a warning now if your ship is not able to handle an upgrade.

This release also contains multiple stability bugfixes, physics performance improvements and many miscellaneous features. Full changelog:

 Re-balanced kinetic damage. Now it's lot easier to destroy a ship - or get destroyed - by breaching reactor with mass-driver bullets.
 New mass-driver fire effect.

 New blueprint-view special effect in upgrades and tuning menu makes descriptions easily readable.

notes.content:
A new year dawns, and with it a new release. Our fist responsibility when making the game - even in early access - is to fix all the bugs and polish up everything first, before implementing new features, so you players get a complete, polished experience. This release attempts to do just that, patching up all the bugs we know about and polishing existing aspects of the game.

The pirate AI got a fine-tune, making them bit less hostile and much easier to scare away. There are now additional accessibility features, and I tried to fix all the bugs I was aware of. There are also new performance improvements and optimizations.

notes.title: December’s Dawn and Dusk
notes.content:
December marks the beginning of a new month with a new focus; but it also marks the last phases of development before we reach version 1.0, closing up all loose threads, completing all the game mechanics and getting something that can be called ‘complete’. We still have a way to go, and I doubt we will be able to wrap it up in 2019, but I’m confident we are just a few months away.

We leave November with new events, such as the Phage-class in-ring refueling station, with new crew system and crew capabilities. Our instruments were refined, Enceladus itself got an overhaul… In total we added 85 new features and polished up 77 details.

And bugs, so many bugs. Over 109 bugs have been reported and fixed. Our diligent community has helped out, submitting logs and savegames that exhibit unusual behavior as a starting point for tracking them down.

So. What’s next?

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33358845/6b82fcc63ea550f4bb75e02c4d7d73899ff739fa.png

Story
December is story month. This is where I begin taking the universe I’ve created into something that lives, breathes, and changes. You’ve already seen many discreet story events in the game, but this is where we begin building real story arcs, events that proceed from events. At the time I’m writing this we have roughly 4 hours of the storyline in, and I want to expand it over to at least 10.

Multiple routes
I intend for stories to have a beginning and an end, yet hopefully still be unique to each play-through, without a single beginning or a single ending, or a single path from any single beginning or ending.  Hopefully, the rings will be a place that you can not only experience, but a place that you can make your mark upon.

New Ships
No doubt you’ve noticed that our favorite K37 is not the only ship maneuvering the rings.  You’ve seen the Search-and-Rescue CERF and the sleek Eagle Prospector plying the rings, but there’s more in the rings, and you’ll begin to see some of these.  Some of these will be other professionals, working the rings just like you.  

Others will be more mysterious, both dangerous and secretive.  Along with new stories being implemented, you’ll see new players in the rings, some of whom may not appreciate the interest you take in their activities. 
 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33358845/c35be6b27ae718b25844ad4d0a9a49113aff0c48.jpg

Ship Dealer
Of course, there’s no cosmic law that you can’t command an Eagle Prospector, or one of the other working vessels plying the rings.  We’ll be opening a ship dealership, allowing the player to get behind the helm of various and varied craft.

Each ship is not simply a better K37, though. Each ship will have its own unique mass balance, its own unique technologies and interfaces, its own unique handling and thrust configurations.  The unique designs, under-the-hood instrumentation, and the physics that influence each ship’s handling will change the personality of each ship on a more fundamental level than changing a value for hit points or increasing a mass value by ten percent. 

The Little Things
As usual, a hundred little details will shift. Improvement and bug fixes will continue, and with the help of a vibrant community, we’ll do all the polishing needed to proudly call the game complete. We will continue to keep the rapid release cycle, so you can still expect to see multiple releases each week in the experimental branch - and few well-tested stable ones as well.

notes.title: 0.137.1 - Enceladian Enterprise
notes.content:
ΔV: Rings of Saturn has come a long way since it’s release in Early Access back in August. We got an overwhelming response from our fanbase, which drove us to release a total of 173 new versions of the game over these 65 days. We’ve averaged almost 3 releases per day - each and every one of them fixing some bugs, improving some aspect of the game and adding new features.

Many of the changes are the result of our community participating in the development of the game. We set up a feature voting system at discord.gg/dv - a way for players to suggest new features, discuss and vote on them. I did my best to add as many of them to the game as I could. Some of these were small improvements, like upgrade suggestions and a new dialog-based tutorial.  Some were huge, game-altering changes.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33358845/f3450e7be4945020a7219ce1361e3f2b3aa7cd8e.png

Our first big player-contributed feature was the addition of the dialog system. A way to directly communicate with other ships was not an intended feature, but it was a very popular request. The comms system allows you now to listen and respond to other ships you encounter in the rings. This gave us the opportunity to flesh out the story and present players with additional, unique quest opportunities.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33358845/8434ec1543c4b0c1400bfb4326b5acf91a16c390.png

The mineral market got a complete overhaul. There are now realistic, long-term price fluctuations. With the addition of geologist predictions, playing the market is a valid way to get (or lose!) funds for your company.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33358845/36395e9a30289cbca3b3d3135aaf41f48b6906e2.png

Our latest large addition is the ability to hire a crew. This fleshes out your company and also gives you additional options on how to run your company. You can hire pilots that will assist you with flying, mechanics that will keep your ship going and geologists that will help you make money from your enterprise.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33358845/02700e3b1d830b4bd7d07500fa45dc09a5fc2780.png

Not all of the changes are huge. Some were just ideas for new upgrades, or ways to tune your ship. We now have a total of 62 upgrades, ranging from additional mining lasers, new reaction control systems, and even drones you can fit on your ship. There were also many small visual polishes - from the way the asteroids fracture under seismic stress, to how camera loses focus if you make sudden zoom, to the way a nuclear exhaust plume interacts with and melts the asteroids. We also got Korean and Norwegian translations of the game.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33358845/e1195717112fd7100518e55787bc99cd2fcd611e.png

We never abandoned our dedication to good, hard science-fiction. With the help of our science-savvy fans, we were able to find and iron out everything that was not up to our standard. Whether it was the plume shape of a thruster not looking realistic enough, or one of the engines breaking conservation of energy, we found all of that and polished it to stand up to the hardest science-fiction standard. And we did get an award to prove that.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33358845/c31b10b7b259f030f172bf32a8801981b9b524dd.png

With the help of our beta-testers and players, we found and squashed literally hundreds of bugs and made dozens of performance optimizations. There are new options for the game allowing you to play on systems that I never expected. The recent addition of fully automated soak tests allowed me to run the game automatically for hours, pinpointing many stability problems that emerge seldom enough to not be apparent in usual testing sessions. As a result, the game is now faster and more stable than ever.

Our usual release notes contain a detailed changelog, and this one will be no different. If you just wanted to know what changed since 0.132.3, here is the detailed list of changes:

 Added crew menu. You can now hire pilots, mechanics, and geologists. Repair, jury-rig, mineral price prediction, and adrenaline capability is now tied to crew stats.
 Geologist will now mark ore chunks on your HUD with estimated composition and value.
 Pilot will now trigger adrenaline automatically if you are on a dangerous course, giving you time to react.
 Changed the way the adrenaline works and its visual effect. Time slowdown is now gradual and your ship always stays in focus.
 You can now fast-travel to Enceladus station.
 Added crew portraits with dynamic lighting.
 Added ability to skip time on Enceladus.
 Significantly improved the performance of the game. There are over 50 optimizations in place, ranging from the physics system, through AI to particle rendering.
 New pixel-doubling option allowing players to artificially lower resolution for both HDPI screens and low-end computers.
 Added Korean and Norwegian translations.
 Changed the way game loads resources. Title screen will not freeze when resources are loaded in the background, and if the game is not fully loaded yet you will get a progress bar.
 Fixed multiple bugs that could crash the game in rare circumstances.

notes.title: October ahead
notes.content:
September changes were all about on-boarding new players. I released 6 new versions (and numerous patched) that added new comms/dialog system, expanded tutorials and captain's logs to aid new players. We also featured a combat review, new camera modes and other quality-of-life improvements.

Since new players got so much attention in September, it's only fair to focus October on our long-time fans.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33358845/eead5a6010a5fc67546f9e4e93ba5b91d20a1f80.png
Crew
I plan to add a crew management mechanic to the game. You will be able to hire a crew - pilot, mechanic, geologist and perhaps others specialists. You'll have a weekly wages to pay, and in exchange the crew will lend in a hand in running your ship and company.

Story
With addition of new dialog system I have a new opportunity to flesh out the story of the game. In October I plan to add at least 3 hours of storyline and some additional hook events to get you going with the story.

Upgrades
At least 20 additional upgrades will be added in October. These will range from new thrusters, mineral processing equipment, exchangeable excavators, different mining tools and drones - up to software upgrades for on-board computer.

Stability
Finally I plan to take extra time to ensure stability of the game. I tracked all the crashes we had to an engine problem that requires a upgrade. The Godot Engine 3.2 (and 3.1.2) is scheduled to release in October and I plan to upgrade to it as soon as it comes out. This will, hopefully, solve all crashes you are experiencing.

notes.title: A road into September
notes.content:
Making games is not hard, but it’s complex. You hardly ever find one big, challenging problem in the development - but you are flooded with multitude of interconnected easy ones. Let’s put this into perspective with numbers: since I begun working on ΔV: Rings of Saturn I added 187 features, fixed 226 bugs and polished up 153 issues.

Since the beginning of Early Access we had 11 public releases, both adding content and patching bugs - and a dozen more for the opt-in beta branch. That’s a new patch every second day on the average.

Where will we go from here? My internal roadmap is similarly detailed - I have 217 issues pending right now, and while they are an excellent help for me, they are far too detailed to show you as general direction game is taking. That’s why I written this roadmap summary of September.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33358845/eead5a6010a5fc67546f9e4e93ba5b91d20a1f80.png
Comms
During a pool at our Discord you decided that you would like to have communications and dialogs with other ships. It’s the privilege of Early Access - players get to decide on direction of development.

Adding a dialogs is a massive feature that changes the game significantly, but you managed to convince me that it will be a huge improvement in the gameplay. I plan to add at least rudimentary dialog system this month.

Expanded tutorials
While many players are enjoying being thrown into deep end, equally many have complained at lack of guidance. I’ll be expanding the tutorial system this month to give a better understanding of the game and what fun things you can do with it.

This feature will take advantage of the comms system to have the tutorial seamlessly integrated into gameplay, without breaking immersion.

Combat review
With all the recent improvements in ships AI and changes in smart camera controls the combat became far more challenging. Sometimes AI’s can snipe you out of the rings before you even see them coming. I’ll be re-viewing the combat scenarios in-depth to make sure the game is challenging but fair at all times.

Captain's logs
A log of things that happened in the game will help you getting up-to-speed after you take a break in the game.

Ringdust
These are big, highly visible features, but you can expect 50 or 60 of tiny things to be changed as well. Small tweaks and features, and of course - bugfixes, polishes and performance improvements. You can re-view each change in release notes accompanying every release.

notes.title: 0.104.7 - White Noise
notes.content:
This is a bugfix release. Bugs fixed:

 Lifepods will no-longer broadcast calls for help on Enceladus dive summary screen.
 Improved performance of lasers and microwaves.
 Reactor will no-longer power up when docked at Enceladus.
 Ships can now have multiple reactors.
 MAD CERF has now twin reactors and you can break them.

notes.title: 0.104.3 - Glowing Hot
notes.content:
This is a hotfix release. It contains small, but important fixes:

 New game used to carry over faction reputation, leading to unexpected behaviour of AI (ie. aggression). Now you begin with clean slate.
 Ship systems don't go mute now when you are on edge of the screen on 4K display.
 Bullets will no-longer hit your excavator if you are flying really fast.
 Updates German translation.
 Fixes typos in various translations.

notes.title: 0.104.1 - Age of Rock
notes.content:
This is a bugfix and polish release, focused on improving stability and gameplay experience. Changes:

 Made miners less likely to fire on you, even if you engaged with them in the past.
 Stability improvements.
 Weapons of K37 will no longer be visible through CERF hull when docking in-ring.
 Fixed a bug that might cause your ship go off-screen on 4K displays.
 You can now control camera by moving the mouse.

notes.title: 0.103.15 - Care Package
notes.content:
This is another bugfix and polishing release. Changelog:

 AI miners are now much more careful when maneuvering near the player.
 Fine-tuned audio for some of the thrusters.
 On-board computer is now harder to damage.
 Long translations will no-longer break the UI.

notes.title: 0.103.14 - Patching Leaks
notes.content:
Following the "fix bug first" paradigm I'm releasing yet another bugfix release. Bugs fixed:

 Fixed a memory leak that caused the game crash when you exited to desktop.
 Changed the way game allocates ships. This should lead to improved stability.
 Game will no-longer crash in the unlikely event of flying out of the mapped area of the rings.
 Fixed a bug that caused upgrade net price to be displayed incorrectly immediately after purchasing new upgrade.
 Fixed dust and smoke effects on Enceladus.

notes.title: 0.103.6 - Hostile Takeovers
notes.content:
This release combines tuning of the AI with bugfixes. Changes:

 AI will not be so hostile anymore. Ship captains will give you some breath if you don't actively shoot them.
 AI can now decide that the best course of action is to just get away from you without provoking further aggression.
 Fixed some causes of crashes, hopefully all of them.
 You can no-longer change camera zoom when game is paused.
 Mass-driver will now shoot properly when underpowered.
 Reactor radiators won't glow through weapons anymore.
 You can now always control OMS screen with a mouse.
 Fixed a bug that caused bullet time carry over to main menu and Enceladus.

notes.title: 0.102.4 - Relaxed Constrains
notes.content:
This is a storytelling enchantment release. A storyteller module of ΔV is the part that keeps the story going - the pirate attacks, the anomalies in the game, bounty hunters patrolling. It was a bit harsh on a new players, and it's tuned now to be more relaxed.

Changes:

 Increased compassion of storyteller module.
 Fixed a but that caused mouse to be blocked when pausing the game while fast-forwarding cutscene.
 Fixed a bug that hid tuning options of mass driver.
 Fixed a bug that caused "launch from Enceladus" sequence to be automatically skipped every time. You can now skip by clicking, or watch it.
 Fixed menu fade at Enceladus Prime when leaving station.

notes.title: 0.101.0 - Singularity Asimptote
notes.content:
Some players argued that ΔV is brutal and hard on the start. This update aims to help with that. It adds an insurance to cover your initial losses when you learn the ropes of the game, and it completely overhauls how the autopilot works.

None of the underlying physics and simulation changed - it's just that some of the on-board system are smarter now.

Changes:

 Complete autopilot overhaul for keyboard+mouse control scheme. Target-locking an object will now cause the autopilot to aim for it automatically, and your movement will be oriented to the object. You can move closer and away from it, and side movement will move you around it. As previously, you will automatically match velocity. It makes it much easier to dig.
 Changed the way camera pans around - it will now show more in the way you are pointing towards (as opposed to showing more in the direction you move), and you can pan around a bit by pointing your mouse at a target. It will also try to maintain anything you target-lock in the shot.
 Added an insurance to cover the repair costs for initial damage of your ship. You need to start a new game to take advantage of it.
 OMS will now work correctly when tutorial is playing.
 Stability improvements. Fixed couple of spots that might cause crashes.

notes.title: Branches of World Ash
notes.content:
You might have noticed that the game comes in three flavors, selectable from your Steam client. Here is what they are all about:

 The default branch contains the version of the game that I think is best suited for general public. This is, as named, the default - and if you don't know what to choose, you should use this.
 The beta branch contains the features that will be soon available, but still need some testing. It's usually a day or two ahead of the default branch and serves as a buffer, so a bug I miss doesn't affect just everybody. Use this branch if you want to see the latest features as soon as I make them. You can opt-in to a #beta-feedback channel on our discord. It's open to anyone who asks, but might contain spoilers. Just ping me if you want access.
 The experimental branch contains features that I'm not sure if they'll make it to the game yet. Game in experimental branch is pretty stable, but contains features that might alter the gameplay dramatically. Experiments usually last for a day or two as I gather feedback, after which this branch will revert back to the default build. Watch the experiments and vote on them on #experimental-feedback channel on our discord.


Questions? Just ask.

notes.title: 0.99.1 - Blindsight
notes.content:
With the release of Early Access you played more game-hours of the game in a single day than our entire betatesting team is able to do in a month. You did find some bugs and some crashes, and this is a first release addressing that.

It's really challenging to find a bug when all I have to work with is "game crashes" - I'm flying blind. I did take a long careful look at the codebase and managed to find some potential issues. Since I had no reliable way to check it, I cannot be sure it helped your case - but I certainly hope they did.

Thank you for your patience, and please let me know if you experience any more bugs. I'l do my best to patch them all up shortly.

Changes:

 New camera controls, giving you more control over manual zoom and doing better job at showing you where are you going.
 Game will no longer crash if you return to main menu and re-load the game.
 Game will not crash if your LIDAR beam hits a asteroid that is just fracturing.
 Game will not crash if beam weapons (lasers, microwaves) hit asteroids that are fracturing due to reasons unrelated to the hit.
 Various other checks for rare conditions that could cause crashes.

notes.title: Release the Perseids
notes.content:
ΔV: Rings of Saturn is all about mining asteroids. That's why we are releasing Early Access on peak of Perseid Meteor Shower, at 12 Aug 2019.

This is a perfect time to discuss where we are now, and where we are going with our development.

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33358845/eead5a6010a5fc67546f9e4e93ba5b91d20a1f80.png

Ringer Edition (you are here)

Complete spaceflight and ringmining simulation
2.5 hours of storyline
Single playable ship
English and Polish language support
Enceladus Prime station:

Upgrade shop with 30 upgrades
Mineral Market
Ship Repairs

Early Access (2019.08.12)
5 hours of storyline
Single playable ship
English and Polish language support
Enceladus Prime station:
50 upgrades
Hiring Crew
Ship tuning

Full Release (~end of 2019)
20 hours of storyline
Three playable ships
Full language support
Enceladus Prime station:

80 upgrades
Ship dealer

Extended Content (for at least a year after release, free for owners of the game)
Additional 5 upgrades every week
5 hours of storyline each month
New ship every two months


You can peek into what I'm currently working on in the #realtime-development-updates channel on our discord.

Can't wait till Perseids? We got you covered.
https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33358845/1361c7b2efa81e832b4bf0c597044d33bb472d58.png

We are releasing the Ringer Edition as a hybrid Early Access / Crowdfunding, giving you and us best of both worlds. What does it mean?
 When you pledge to Rings of Saturn you will immediately get a game to play. No waiting for beta or early access, you can download playable game right now.
 You can choose from all the nice backer perks and influence the direction the game is developing on our discord server right now.
 Even if we don't meet the goals, we will finish the game just as planned. It will just take bit longer, as I have to run other projects simultaneously for funding.
 You also get a Early Access Steam key with Perseids.

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33358845/a3fd6dadc37c8bc8e0e28ab4c8824ee10784cfeb.png
So what is this Ringers Edition?

Game is still in development, but it's fully playable. There are no placeholders, everything that is in game looks just like it will look in finished game. We are still working on adding new content and new mechanics of the game.

With Ringer Edition you get immediate access to the game, completely DRM free and available on all platforms. You will also get a Steam Early Access key with the Perseids.

Interested? Check details of our Early Crowd Ringers Edition here. 

Or - if you prefer - just wait for Perseids. It will be a sight to see.

Changelog:

 Added new hypervelocity impact visual effects.
 Added motion blur for fast-moving projectiles.
 Added audio feedback for LIDAR.

notes.title: 0.74.1 - Hardened Science
notes.content:
Hardcore sci-fi fans might have noticed that propellant consumption of the K37 Nuclear Thermal Rocket was not really realistic - not given the description of the ships reactor, it's temperature and physics. In recent days we worked, with significant help from our players, on fixing that - but maintaining good gameplay experience at the same time.

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33358845/ab81f161f364216f031de2ae798137451f54e98e.gif

Today I can present you the fruit of this: Re-balanced Boosted Nuclear Thermal Rocket. This version changes exhaust velocities, power consumption and propellant tank sizes - and a required a significant improvement in the autopilot. It's now much smarter, able to assess ship's inertia and uses thrusters only when required to conserve your propellant. It's also much better at aiming now.

The re-balance introduced new, interesting gameplay element. Your ship will now behave differently as your propellant tanks empty. As your total mass reduces the ship will get agile and speedy - unless you manage to fill up the cargo hold. I hope you will enjoy it as much as we did.

Savegame compatibility note: This version includes new, bigger, propellant tanks that will not be compatible with your old save. You might use that save, but you will need to buy propellant tank to get the ship running.

Changelog:

 New NTR setup for all ships equipped with Nuclear Thermal Rockets.
 New fuel tank upgrades accommodating higher propellant consumption.
 Significantly improved autopilot control.
 Speed-up VFX will no longer flash for one frame at beginning of the game.

notes.title: 0.63.3 - I find your lack of updates disturbing
notes.content:
Development of every commercial game consists not only of making the game itself, but also many assorted tasks, that are not directly visible to you players. Things like negotiating agreements, securing financing, handling marketing and other boring yet required stuff. They took over the recent month, but it's now time to get actual game update.

0.63.3 is a fix/re-balance release. Changelog:

 Upgraded Godot Engine to 3.1.1.
 Made sure that ship won't hit anything during initial cutscene.
 Re-balanced damage to thrusters and reactor. It's now harder to get choke and leak.
 Fixed OMS being to dark in presence of shiny crystals.

notes.title: 0.62.1 - The Paint Job
notes.content:
This release adds the very first modding opportunity to ΔV. Now your ship can have a custom paint job (also in beta!). Changelog:

 Adds basic modding suport.
 Adds custom paint job for Rosatom-Antonov K37-TNTRL
 New high-resolution lifepod.


https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33358845/bb1fcbc5a7132a4d2e4b1aa526903695e0715545.gif

The modding feature is still very fresh. For mod instructions please join our workshop discord channel.

notes.title: 0.61.6 - Sky is the Limit
notes.content:
A few versions back I accidentally removed the time limit of the demo version of the game. Since there was no ill effect of this, I might as well make it official - there is no artificial time limit in the demo version now.

This release includes some additional fixes:

 Improved performance of story elements.
 Fixed line-of-sight glitches on very wide displays.
 Officially removed time limit of the demo.

notes.title: 0.61.4 - Quantum Leap
notes.content:
This is a bugfix release. Changes:

 Exhaust gas simulation is no longer affected by adrenaline boost induced bullet-time.
 Fixed "exit to main menu" option on demo end screen.
 Game loading now faster by 40%.
 Adjusted density of the rings.
 Fine-tuned the tutorial display options to be more readable.
 Lights on Enceladus no-linger blind the camera for dive summary screen.
 Fixes audio on boot splash.

notes.title: 0.61.0 - Guiding Hand
notes.content:
This release expands the in-game tutorial. Changelog:

 Added recon drone tutorial section, covering camera controls and mining.
 Improved LIDAR display readability.
 Added motion blur effect when zooming in/out rapidly.
 Changed they way tutorial works to allow multiple independent tutorials covering different parts of the game.
 Fixed some audio issues with boot splash.

notes.title: 0.60.2 - Minor Adjustments
notes.content:
This release improves upon tutorial and brings in some additional gameplay balancing. Changelog:

 Improved the way tutorial detects player actions.
 Changed active time and cooldown time of adrenaline booster to make it more playable.

notes.title: 0.60.1 - Manual Operation
notes.content:
This release brings in often-requested tutorial. It's quite basic right now, but will be expanded as necessary to cover all confusing aspects of gameplay. Changelog:

 Adds basic tutorial for game controls.
 Tiny asteroids will no longer flicker on edge of gravitational disturbance.
 Mineral Market and Ship Repairs screen will no-longer overflow small displays.
 Mineral Market now has a scroll on small displays.
 Alarm siren will no longer fire in cutscenes.

notes.title: 0.58.2 - Thread of Compatibility
notes.content:
This is a bugfix release. Changes:

 Game will no-longer crash to desktop on Linux systems.
 You can skip the boot splash also with mouse click now.

notes.title: 0.58.1 - Glimpse of Freedom
notes.content:
This release adds boot splash and fixes some bugs. Changelog:

 Added a boot screen that plays an animation while game loads resources.
 Fixed bug that caused weapons that are not installed show up on the OMS screen.

notes.title: 0.57.2 - Collecting Debris
notes.content:
This is a bugfix release. Bugs fixed:

 Changing HUD size no-longer causes camera to zoom in and out.
 Fixes damage display in OMS screen.
 Debt is correctly displayed now in Enceladus.
 All damage to on-board computer can be fixed now.
 Fixing ship on Enceladus is now immediately visible in game.
 Fixes alternate ending in "Flight for Rescue" storyline.

notes.title: 0.57.1 - Stabilizing Vision
notes.content:
Recent release of stable version of Godot Engine 3.1 removed an important roadblock for release ΔV. As of now the game no-longer uses a bleeding-edge unstable game engine! Changelog:

 Upgraded game engine to latest, stable version of Godot 3.1
 Enabled new rendering feature that should improve performance on Radeon GPUs.
 Adjusted ship lighting.
 Added additional elements to title screen to prevent boredom should you like to hear title theme to the end.
 Fixed a  bug that caused game to crash-to-desktop when your ship was destroyed.
 Added additional story elements.

notes.title: 0.55.1 - Branching Tales
notes.content:
This release expands module responsible for story of the game. Stories can now have branches and progression. Changelog:

 Added ability to branch storyline.
 Stories can now have long-lasting events, as long as there is a player to observe it.
 Lifepod will no-longer blind the ships camera.
 Made sure that ships going on rescue missions have sufficient propellant to preform the rescue.

notes.title: 0.55.0 - Damage and Repairs
notes.content:
This update changes the way damage and repairs are handled. Changelog:

 System damage is more forgiving. No system should be damaged completely beyond scope of jury-rigging on the first hit.
 Fixed a nasty bug that caused no damage being dealt from kinetic impacts to ships.
 You cannot damage the ship beyond 100% now.

notes.title: 0.54.2 - Applying Polish
notes.content:
This is a bugfix release. Changes:

 Removes audible clicks from Morse code transmissions.
 Updated German translation.
 Improved performance of collision detection.

notes.title: 0.54.0 - Variable Thrust
notes.content:
This release bring forth improvements to lower layer of autopilot/AI software of the ship. Changes:

 New autopilot software mk2 is aware ot the thruster placement and alignements and will avoid firing thrusters that cancel each-other out. This causes significantly better propellant efficiency when flying autopilot.
 Machines Astro-Dynamiques Cerunnos Modèle II got an variable thrust engines, which in conjunction with new autopilot allows faster and more precise docking/rescue maneuvers.
 You can no longer break thrusters/CPU due to collision with your own cargo in cargo hold.

notes.title: 0.53.0 - Spinning Tales
notes.content:
This release focuses on storytelling improvements. Changelog:

 Changed the way the storytelling module chains story episodes to avoid clustering of similar events. This should make the dynamic story more interesting.
 Fixed a bug that could cause crash to desktop if AI shoot a helpless ship by accident.

notes.title: 0.52.0 - Positive Feedback Loop
notes.content:
This release includes often-requested bloom setting for the game. I also fine-tuned AI settings so ships are no-longer paralyzed by fear in the rings and added additional story elements to both beta and demo versions.

Changelog:

 Big ships will no longer be paralyzed in presence of multiple small rocks.
 Rescue ships will now perform rescue even in presence of small asteroids.
 Adjusted docking clamps for MAD CERF to allow full rotation of the docking ships.
 Adjusted autopilot settings for MAD CERF so it will no longer spin out of control when it has damaged thrusters.
 Polished up the lifepods.
 Added setting to turn off the bloom/glow.
 Added 4 additional story events.

notes.title: 0.51.2 - Bay of Pirates
notes.content:
This quick follow-up patch beefs up pirate AI behaviour. Changelog:

 AI Pirates are now better at making traps.
 Performance improvements in bigger battles.
 AI can no-longer become hostile to it's own faction due to friendly fire.

notes.title: 0.51.1 - Light of Change
notes.content:
This is a complementary bugfix release to 0.51.0. Fixes:

 Fixed auto-exposure settings so bright flashes from emergency lights of lifepods won't blind the camera for too long any more.
 Fixed lighting settings for Enceladus Prime station.
 Reduced number random encounters on the edge of the ring.

notes.title: 0.51.0 - Call for Help
notes.content:
With this update I added a new ship for both demo and beta versions of the game and expanded storyline. Full changelog:


 Added Machines Astro-Dynamiques Cerunnos Modèle II (aka "CERF") ring rescue ship.
 AI can now find broken ships, pilot a rescue ship to them and drive them out of the rings safely.
 When you end up helpless in the ring (with no power, propellant or critically damaged ship), an AI ship will show up to pick you up and tow you to safety.
 You now have a chance to encounter rescue operation within the Ring.
 Lifepods are now equipped with emergency radio beacon.
 AI Pirates can now use lifepods to lure victims into traps.
 You will now automatically sell anomalies that have no other function upon returning to Enceladus Prime station.

notes.title: 0.50.1 - Survival Principles
notes.content:
This version add lifepods to the game. Changelog:

 Player-controlled ship can now leave lifepod behind.
 You can find lifepods in the rings and rescue them.
 Fine-tuned excavation AI.

notes.title: 0.49.0 - For Ringalowda!
notes.content:
This release further expands AI of the ships in the game. I refined the mineral-catching behaviour, added excavation logic and fine-tuned all the parameters. Specific changes:

 AI ships can now dig up the minerals themselves.
 Ships will now value their life more, abandoning output in grave danger.
 Fixed amount of propellant in AI controlled ships, so they don't run dry so quickly.
 Ships will now return to the station when they are low on propellant.
 AI will no longer use all the power just for defense, leaving them drifting helplessly.

notes.title: 0.48.0 - Account of Greed
notes.content:
This is AI enhancement release. AI is now aware of values of minerals and will attempt to catch valuable ones. Changes include:

 Taught AI how to catch mineral asteroids.
 AI now is aware of value of minerals.
 Fixed bug in AI that caused it to loose orientation if there were no asteroids nearby.
 When AI is flying towards an object it wants to observe or catch, it will now take it's velocity into account.
 Re-modeled physical model for excavator to allow AI to accurately assess it's position.

notes.title: 0.47.4 - The Void Guard
notes.content:
This is a bugfix release. Changes:

 Game will no longer crash when target of AI leaves detailed simulation zone around the player.
 Damage from energy weapons is now considered an hostile act.

notes.title: 0.46.1 - Micro Waves
notes.content:
Resuming the development after a short vacations. Changes in this version:


 Microwave Emitter weapon is now visible on ships equipped with it.
 Ionized ringdust plasma from Microwave Emitter is now (barely) visible to naked eye.
 Updated the engine to latest version.

notes.title: 0.45.1 - Once upon a Time
notes.content:
This version introduces storytelling-subsystem - the part of the game in charge of telling the story. It still has very few story elements to choose from, but it's an important milestone in development.

Full changelog:

 Added a storytelling system.
 Added 4 new story elements.
 Fine-tuned HUD display of LIDAR.
 High-energy impacts now can cause explosion.

notes.title: 0.44.0 - Cogs of Wisdom
notes.content: 0.44.0 brings significantly improved AI. Computer-controlled ships can now plot a valid course, avoid obstacles and now maneuver with great propellant efficiency.

notes.title: 0.43.3 - Insecticide
notes.content:
This is a bugfix release. Changes:

 Adjusted mass driver mountpoint for K37.
 Reactor radiators light now correctly affect the damaged parts of the ship.
 You can no longer crash into asteroids during cutscene.
 Repairing your ship now resets jury-rig levels.
 Propellant mist on Enceladus now appears correctly around the ship when disconnecting fuel lines during launch sequence.

notes.title: 0.43.0 - Drive of the Mass
notes.content:
This release restores visibility of weapons in game. It required re-design of all the weapons so they no-longer obscure the excavator. Full changelog:

 Weapons are now visible in-game.
 Improved performance of large, high-speed asteroid impacts.

notes.title: 0.42.4 - Sky is the Limit
notes.content:
This is a bugfix release. Fixes:

 You can now own more than 100 tons of H2O.
 Fixed weird focus behaviour when navigating the Enceladus menu with gamepad.

notes.title: 0.42.3 - Hotfix
notes.content: This is a hotfix release that fixes crash-to-desktop caused by opening ship repair menu after selling many minerals.

notes.title: 0.42.2 - Damage Control
notes.content:
Version 0.42.2 adds ship repair menu to Enceladus Prime station. You can now inspect ship damage and fix or replace broken parts. Replacement costs much more, but takes less time and completely fixes the broken system, while fixing sacrifices additional time and quality for lower price.

Changelog:

 Added ship repair menu in Enceladus Prime station.
 Improved camera movement inside Enceladus Prime station.
 Visual and performance fixes.

notes.title: 0.41.0 - Rust Bucket
notes.content:
Fist post-Christmas release comes with visual improvement and further expansion of Enceladus Prime station. Changes:

 Damage and wear is now directly visible on the ship.
 Added pre-flight inspections on Enceladus Prime.
 Launch sequence will no longer crash ship into the station when some of the thrusters are broken.
 Fixed mineral market hiding out of the screen on vertical-oriented displays.

notes.title: 0.40.0 - Market Fluctuations
notes.content:
Version 0.40.0 further expands Enceladus Prime station, but also improves few aspects of the demo. Changelog:

 Upgraded game engine to latest version.
 There is now a fully functional Mineral Market at Enceladus Prime station. You can buy and sell various minerals.
 Added basic market simulation - prices of minerals change over time.
 Polished appearance of certain anomalies.
 Adjusted lighting settings (again).

notes.title: 0.39.0 - Damage Potential
notes.content:
Version 0.39.0 brings additional ways in which you can damage - and fix - your ship. Changes include:

 Thrusters can now be chocked by well-aimed impact.
 Overheating reactor might now cause turbine galling.
 On-board computer can now have damaged sensor connections, can overheat or short-circuit.
 Fixed clicking sound when ship is out of fuel.
 You can no-longer enter OMS mode in cutscene.

notes.title: 0.38.0 - Expanding Horizons
notes.content:
Main feature of 0.38.0 release is an expanded compatibility with Radeon cards. I could not do this without your - community - support, especially Blaank from our Discord server, who contributed many hours of his time to help me pinpoint the problems. Thank you!

Changes include:

 Improved compatibility with Radeon cards.
 Generally improved framerate for Enceladus Prime screen.
 Fixed ship boot / launch sequence.
 Fine-tuned the new soundtrack.

notes.title: 0.37.0 - Moving Forward
notes.content:
Version 0.37.0 focuses on expanding post-demo gameplay. Demo is kept in-sync at all times, so even if you have no access to additional content you will see all the related improvements. Changes:

 Game has a clock now.
 Company funds counter at Enceladus Prime station.
 Adds dive summary/sell screen at Enceladus Prime.
 Added more detailed graphics for minerals.
 Added shaders to minerals to make pure metals look reflective.
 New music track.
 Fixes clicking sound when ship is out of propellant.

notes.title: 0.34.2 fine-tuning hot-fix
notes.content:
A quick follow up to 0.34.1, with following changes:

 OMS now appears instantly after keypress.
 Jury-rig menu can be fully operated with gamepad.
 Fine-tuned lighting effects bit more.

notes.title: 0.34.1 is available for download!
notes.content:
This is a feature version. Changes:

 Mid-flight jury-rig menu fully operational! Now you have a skilled mechanic who can fix up things for you when you play.
 Fine-tuned auto-exposure and glow effects.
 Small fixes in Spanish translation.

notes.title: 0.33.0 - Spanish language pack
notes.content:
Changes:

 Added Spanish language (by Emiliano Domenech).
 Increase background music variety.

notes.title: 0.32.4 hotfix
notes.content:
A quick follow-up to 0.32.2 fixes few issues introduced in previous versions, as well as some general improvements:

 Fixed broken settings menu visuals.
 Remastered all music tracks.
 Navigation in menu with keyboard and gamepad much more visible.
 Fine-tuned bloom and lighting effects.
 Fine-tuned UI sound effects.
 New spotlight for the ship.

notes.title: 0.32.2 performance bugfix
notes.content:
0.32.2 is a bugfix edition. Bugs fixed:

 Significantly improved performance on Radeon GPU chipsets.
 Menu buttons are now clickable on the edges.
 Hitting cancel button on the keyboard definition screen now cancels active key capture.

notes.title: 0.32.1 - the sounds in space
notes.content:
Version 0.32.1 features number of sound improvements:

 Added additional soundtrack to dynamic sound mixing module.
 Added sounds to UI.
 You can no longer switch tabs in the setting menu when it's closed.
 Adjusted some abnormal cargo, so it can now be safely loaded on-board.

notes.title: 0.30.1 performance hotfix
notes.content: 0.30.1 hotfix is up, which fixes performance problems when multiple ships were visible on screen.

notes.title: 0.30.0 published
notes.content:
Changes:

 Expanded HUD of the autopilot to show engagement and velocities.
 Added some context-sensitive tutorial hints to the game.
 Adrenaline booster key now can be assigned in the menu.
 Fixed problem with settings windows closing when user clicked outside of them loosing settings.
 Changed the default keymapping.
 There is maximum 5 keys you can bind to an action now.
 Cosmetic changes to the menus.
 LIDAR display window will no longer be stretched.

notes.title: 0.29.1 published
notes.content:
Version 0.29.1 published, featuring:

 Added in-game keyboard mapping editor.
 Added community-supplied French translation by Augur.
 Fine-tuned sound effects for jury-rig menu.
 Fixed text missing from in-game HUD.

notes.title: 0.27.1 performance hotfix
notes.content: This version significantly improves performance and framerates of the game on all systems.

notes.title: v0.27.0 is out!
notes.content:
Changelog:

 New parallax foreground for improved ring depth effect.
 Added a stronger spotlight for navigating in the shadows.
 Fixed bullet time / adrenaline booster sounding the ship-wide alarm when activated.
 Added Onboard Maintenance System view (no mechanic in the demo yet, sorry!)

notes.title: v0.26.3: Hotfix edition
notes.content: This hotfix edition fixes the demo crash-to-desktop problem when demo is about to end.

notes.title: v0.26.2 released
notes.content:
Features:

 Added nuclear reactor leaks and permanent thruster damage.
 Upgraded the engine to latest version.
 Fixed large rocks doing far too much damage to the ship.
 Ship's electric turbine consumes reactive mass now and will shut down when ship is empty.
 Fixed missing executable icons for Windows builds.
 You can no longer un-pause the game using gamepad when settings menu is open.
 Fine-tuned background milky way display.

notes.title: v0.24.5
notes.content:
Today I published 0.24.5 bugfix release. Changes:

 Fixed shadow rendering bug near large asteroids.
 Fixed full-screen window flickering on Linux in settings screen.
 Fixed incorrect music track playing during high-g maneuvers.
 Adjusted auto-exposure settings.

notes.title: v0.24.2
notes.content:
ΔV: Rings of Saturn v0.24.2 just got released. This is player-feedback based release, with improvements gathered all around community. Changes:

 Demo timer extended by 300%.
 Added emergency heat venting for on-board computer. It will prevent meltdown, as long as it is powered.
 Exposed the adrenaline booster life-support addon.
 Added button to return to main menu and play again after demo ends.

These changes were all suggested by players, either directly, or gathered from gameplay videos you posted. Thank you everyone for the feedback!

notes.title: v0.23.1
notes.content:
ΔV: Rings of Saturn v0.23.1 just got released. Features:

 Game is now on full-screen by default.
 Added colorblind mode.
 Camera zoom now reacts much faster on both mouse and gamepad.
 Improved performance.
 Visual tuning of background rocks.
